Window Mirror Tint Legality

Whilst mirrored window tinting provides the least visibility to people outside your vehicle, this is not a feasible option in Australia. This is because reflectance for car window tinting is limited to just 10% (the standard for untreated glass). These laws are in place to protect you and others on the road as windows with a higher reflectivity may impair the vision of drivers and lead to accidents.

Darkest Legal Tint

The darkest legal tint allowed varies depending on the vehicle’s type and the window’s location. In Victoria, for passenger vehicles, the darkest legal tint is one that allows a minimum of 35% of light to pass through the window. This is often referred to as a “35% tint”. For the front windscreen, only a clear or very light tint is allowed above the AS1 line or the topmost 10% of the windscreen.

The good news though, is that you don’t need to worry about accidentally breaking this requirement with Tint a Car’s darkest legal tint films, as we’ve researched for you!
